summary: @wethenorth12/etherjs postinstall harvests installer credentials and exfiltrates to Telegram bot and hardcoded C2
details: The package impersonates ethers.js (name '@wethenorth12/etherjs', description 'Complete Ethereum library and wallet implementation', author 'ricmoo') and runs a postinstall.js script at npm install time. The script enumerates installer-owned secret locations (~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, ~/.gitconfig, Chrome/Firefox profile paths including Cookies, Login Data, key4.db, and crypto-wallet directories) and reads a hardcoded list of credential-shaped environment variables (NPM_TOKEN, NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_*, *_PRIVATE_KEY, MNEMONIC, SEED_PHRASE, and others). The collected data is transmitted via GET to api.telegram.org using a hardcoded bot token and chat_id, and via POST to /collect on 40f955f39128bd79-178-249-214-24.serveousercontent.com. Both destinations are attacker-controlled and unrelated to any documented purpose of an Ethereum library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
